gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the in-ear Liberty 4 Pro's '10 h' battery rating is with noise cancelling off. Headphonecheck ran the same test (AAC, high volume) on all three. It measured 6.5 h for the Liberty 4 Pro with ANC at maximum, against 9 h for each of the open-ear AeroFit 2 and Bose Ultra Open. So once you use the noise cancelling that is the reason to buy in-ear, the open-ear models run about 38% longer per charge.
standout_why: The saved ChatGPT chat ran no searches and cited no pages, so there were no rival pages to compare against. The only thing to compare is its own answer, a table of category traits ('Long-term comfort: Often better', 'Noise cancellation: Often excellent') with no battery numbers and no test conditions. Nowhere does it say that in-ear battery claims are rated with ANC off, that Bose rates its battery at 75 dBA pink noise, or that turning on spatial audio (Bose Immersive Audio) roughly halves the runtime.
decides: The finding backs the open-ear pick for the 'wear it 6–8 hours a day' shopper, and shows the in-ear advantage is conditional. An in-ear pair outlasts open-ear only with ANC off (Liberty 4 Pro 10 h vs 9 h, Headphonecheck). With ANC on, the in-ear falls below a full workday (6.5 h Headphonecheck; 5 h 42 min SoundGuys), while AeroFit 2 and Bose Ultra Open each reach 9 h on the same test. Bose's spatial-audio mode is the exception among open-ear models: 4.5 h by Bose's own figure, 5 h by Headphonecheck. Footnote for the table: battery hours = same lab, same codec, same 'high volume'; in-ear shown with ANC on, Bose shown with Immersive Audio off and on.
